statement: Consider the complete graph on the vertex set {1, 2, ..., 8}. Give the edge {i, j} (with i < j) the weight j - i if i + j is odd, and the weight -1 if i + j is even. The weight of a perfect matching is the product of the weights of its four edges. Find the sum of the weights of all 105 perfect matchings of this graph.
Find the number of ordered pairs (a, b) of positive integers with a <= 2026 and b <= 2026 such that ab + 1 divides a^2 + b^2.
Consider the 36 points (x, y) in the plane with x, y in {0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5}. How many triangles with positive area have all three of their vertices among these 36 points?

A fair coin is flipped repeatedly until either the sequence HTHHT or the sequence THTHH appears as five consecutive flips. The probability that HTHHT appears first can be written as m/n in lowest terms. Find m + n.

Consider the graph whose 27 vertices are the points (x, y, z) with x, y, z in {0, 1, 2}, where two points are adjacent when they differ by exactly 1 in exactly one coordinate. A particle starts at (0, 0, 0). Each second it moves to a neighbor of its current vertex chosen uniformly at random. The expected number of seconds until the particle first reaches (2, 2, 2) can be written as m/n in lowest terms. Find m + n.

A bracelet has 12 beads equally spaced around a circle. Each bead is red, green, or blue, and exactly 4 beads have each color. Two bracelets are considered the same if one can be turned into the other by a rotation or a reflection. How many different bracelets are there?
How many subsets of {1, 2, ..., 20}, including the empty set, have a sum of elements that is divisible by 7?
How many permutations p of {1, 2, ..., 11} satisfy p(i) != i and |p(i) - i| <= 2 for every i in {1, 2, ..., 11}?

A game starts with a pile of n stones. Two players alternate turns. On each turn the player to move removes exactly 2, 3, or 7 stones from the pile; a move that would remove more stones than remain is not allowed. A player who cannot make a move loses. For how many integers n with 1 <= n <= 2026 does the player who moves first lose, assuming both players play perfectly?
Define a sequence by a_1 = 1 and a_(n+1) = a_n + floor(sqrt(a_n)) for n >= 1. Find the index n for which a_n = 2^20.
In how many ways can a 3 x 12 rectangle be tiled completely, with no overlaps, by 1 x 2 dominoes (placed in either orientation) and 2 x 2 squares?

2026 people stand in a circle, numbered 1 to 2026 clockwise. Starting with person 1 and going clockwise, they count off 1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3, ..., skipping anyone already eliminated; every person who says 3 is eliminated (so persons 3, 6, 9, ... are the first to leave). The counting continues around the circle until exactly one person remains. What is that person's number?
How many lattice paths from (0, 0) to (12, 12) use only unit steps to the right (+1, 0) and up (0, +1), and never visit a point (x, y) with |x - y| > 2?
Compute the sum of floor(k^2 / 2029) over k = 1, 2, ..., 2028.

In how many ways can the 16 cells of a 4 x 4 grid be colored using the three colors red, green, and blue so that no two cells sharing an edge have the same color? Not every color needs to be used, and colorings that differ by a rotation or reflection of the grid count as different.
